newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia cuts interest rate on loans, deposits.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia cuts interest rate on loans, deposits.

text.p: The central National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) said on Thursday it had cut interest charged by commercial banks on loans and deposits to stimulate investment.

The NBE said in a statement it had reduced interest on commercial bank loans to 10.5 percent from 16 percent and had cut interest on deposits to 7.0 percent from 10 percent. The changes were effective from September 16, it said.
The central bank said the reduction in bank loans was meant to inspire more people to turn to commercial banks for loans, promote bank deposits and spur investment.
"The new policy was also aimed at discouraging those who simply deposit money in banks and live on interest to think about investment on any business venture," the bank said.
Ethiopian economists and bankers said the new interest policy was bound to drastically affect newly established private banks with small capital that survived on interest from loans.

Three private banks have been launched in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa and have established branches throughout the country since Prime Minister Meles Zenawi's government liberalised the country's financial system in 1994.
These include the Awash Bank, the Dashen Bank and Bank of Abyssinia. All are fully owned by Ethiopian shareholders.
